planting.note: Start seeds indoors or direct sow after last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Intenz bears vivid purple-red, slender wheat-type flower spikes on a heat-tolerant summer annual.

directions: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting, or direct sow after last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Intenz bears slender, upright, vividly saturated purple-red flower spikes in the narrow wheat-celosia form, opening on sturdy stems that hold up well as fresh or dried cut flowers, and blooms from summer through frost with heat tolerance that keeps it flowering through the hottest part of the Gulf South growing season. Its intense color and long, straight stems make it a strong performer in a cutting garden. Deadhead or cut spent stems to encourage continued branching and flowering, and expect some self-sowing if seed heads are left in place.

common_name: Pink Zazzle Gomphrena (Large Ball-Form Bright Pink Globe Amaranth)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting, or direct sow after last frost in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Pink Zazzle bears unusually large, bright pink, ball-shaped flower heads.

directions: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun. Pink Zazzle bears notably large, rounded, vivid bright pink flower heads, bigger than standard globe amaranth blooms, on a compact, well-branched plant that flowers continuously from summer through frost with no deadheading required, since spent heads dry naturally on the plant. It is among the most reliable Gulf South summer annuals for sustained bloom through brutal heat and humidity that collapses many other bedding plants, and it draws butterflies readily. Excellent as a fresh or dried cut flower, with the dried flower heads holding color for months.

common_name: Tricolor Sweet Potato Vine (Pink-White-Green Variegated Ornamental Vine)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container plants after the last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Tricolor bears leaves variegated in pink, white, and green, a softer, pastel counterpart to solid-colored ornamental sweet potato vine cultivars.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings or container plants after the last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; some afternoon shade helps preserve the pink and white variegation from bleaching out in the hottest sun. Tricolor bears heart-shaped leaves splashed in pink, cream-white, and green, a softer, pastel-toned variegation pattern distinct from the solid chartreuse of Marguerite or the near-black of Blackie, cascading readily over container edges or spreading as a dense groundcover. Its unusual color combination pairs well with pink or white-flowered companion annuals in mixed plantings. In zone 9, the storage tubers sometimes survive mild winters in protected positions, though it is typically grown as a warm-season annual.
